sentences.text:
Mr. P. Roy Barman vs Mr. B. Majumder on 8 August, 2024
Author: T. Amarnath Goud

Bench: T. Amarnath Goud
 Page 1 of 2
 High Court Of Tripura
 _A_G_A_R_T_A_L_A_
 Wp(C) No.521 of 2024
For Petitioner(s) : Mr. P. Roy Barman, Sr. Advocate.
 Ms. A. Debbarma, Advocate.

For Respondent(s) : Mr. B. Majumder, Deputy Sgi.
Hon'Ble Mr. Justice T. Amarnath Goud _O_ R_ D_ E_ R_ 08.08.2024 Heard.

The present petition has been filed under Article-226 of the Constitution of India for directing the respondent to appoint arbitrator for determining the amount of compensation for acquiring land measuring 0.012 acres.

The petitioner has prayed for the following reliefs:
"i. Issue rule upon the respondents to show cause as to why a writ in the nature of mandamus and/or order/orders and/or direction/directions of like nature shall not be issued whereby directing the respondents to appoint an arbitrator for determining the amount of compensation for acquiring land measuring 0.012 acres in terms of Section-3G(5) of the National Highways Act, 1956 in connection with L.A. Case No.11/SDR/2023, apportionment No.63(i), for the purpose of construction of Western Bye-Pass road connecting to NH-8 to NH-108B.
ii. Call for records.
iii. Make rules absolute."
The facts in brief are that the petitioner is the owner of land measuring 0.012 acres (Bastu, Nal class of land), having exclusive right, title, interest and possession over the said land.

The Addl. DM&
Collector, West Tripura, Agartala, in respect of L.A. Case No.11/SDR/2023 apportionment No. 63(i)

has informed the petitioner that land measuring 0.012 acres (Bastu, Nal) has been acquired by the Govt. of India under the National Highway Act, for5 the purpose of construction of Western Bye-Pass road connecting to NH-8 to NH-108B Land Acquisition Collector, West Tripura, Agartala,
in connection with L.A. Case No.11/SDR/2023.

The petitioner was also informed that has been Mr. P. Roy Barman vs Mr. B. Majumder on 8 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190918773/
1 considered eligible to get compensation @Rs.7,26,522/- towards acquiring the aforesaid land.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On 16.01.2024, the petitioner has submitted a representation regarding objection on quantum of compensation award against acquisition of land but till date no arbitrator has been appointed by the respondents for in terms of Section-3G(5) of the Act, 1956.
Being aggrieved by the conduct of the respondents, the petitioner has filed the present writ petition before this Court for redress.

In view of above and having heard the learned counsel appearing for the parties, without going into the merits of the case, this Court finds that the representation regarding objection submitted by the petitioner is not recognized under the statute and thus, liberty is given to the petitioner to file an appropriate application invoking arbitration clause under the Act and on receipt of such application,
the respondent shall consider the same in accordance with law as expeditiously as possible preferably within a period of four months from the date of receipt of the copy of the application.
Accordingly, the present writ petition stands disposed of.
As a sequel, miscellaneous application pending, if any, shall stand closed.
T. AMARNATH GOUD, J A. Ghosh ANJAN
Digitally signed by  ANJAN GHOSH GHOSH
